    Warren v. The Children's Hospital Corporation (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca1-23-01158 / USCOURTS-ca1-23-01158-0

    FAPD-AI: Dr. Luigi Warren co-invented an mRNA reprogramming technology while employed at the Immune Disease Institute and disputes which royalty-sharing policy applies to his Moderna licensing agreement. The Children's Hospital Corporation applied its own policy instead of the IDI policy, reducing Warren's compensation. The appeals court vacated the lower court's summary judgment on the breach of contract claim, finding factual disputes regarding whether the IDI policy was binding and whether it could be retroactively amended. USCOURTS-SEL-01

    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca3-25-02546 / USCOURTS-ca3-25-02546-0

    FAPD-AI: The Third Circuit reversed a district court's application of Younger abstention and held that the National Shooting Sports Foundation has Article III standing to challenge New Jersey's A1765 firearms statute after the state commenced six enforcement actions against gun industry members, including some NSSF members.     Center for Taxpayer Rights, et al v. IRS, et al (opens in a new tab)

    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca5-24-30552 / USCOURTS-ca5-24-30552-0

    FAPD-AI: IFG Port sued Lake Charles Harbor Terminal District over responsibility for ship channel dredging permits; a magistrate judge awarded IFG nearly $125 million. After judgment, the Port discovered the magistrate judge and IFG's lead counsel had a close 40-year personal friendship that was inadequately disclosed before the parties consented to the referral. The court affirmed vacation of the referral, holding the Port's consent was not knowing. USCOURTS-SEL-01

  • Observed at 16:54:04 Eastern time ET
    USA v. Antonio Carrow (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca11-25-13650 / USCOURTS-ca11-25-13650-0

    FAPD-AI: Carrow appealed his 24-month sentence imposed for revocation of supervised release following violations including drug use and unauthorized residence changes. The court affirmed the sentence, rejecting claims that it was procedurally or substantively unreasonable, finding the District Court considered appropriate sentencing factors and Carrow failed to establish plain error. USCOURTS-SEL-01

  • Observed at 16:54:04 Eastern time ET
    USA v. Gabriel Lee (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca11-25-13881 / USCOURTS-ca11-25-13881-0

    FAPD-AI: Lee appealed denial of his motion to reconsider a sentence reduction under Amendment 833 to the Sentencing Guidelines. The court affirmed, finding Amendment 833 was not made retroactive by the Sentencing Commission and thus was not available for sentence reduction motions. USCOURTS-SEL-01

  • Observed at 16:54:03 Eastern time ET
    USA v. Judy Owen (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca11-25-11657 / USCOURTS-ca11-25-11657-0

    FAPD-AI: The appellant was convicted of murder for hire, conspiracy to commit murder for hire, and firearm transfer in connection with a plan by her and her sisters to hire someone to kill a man over a child custody dispute. The scheme involved multiple failed attempts with different hired individuals. The Eleventh Circuit affirmed her convictions and 120-month sentence, rejecting her arguments regarding insufficiency of evidence and prosecutorial comment on her right to remain silent. USCOURTS-SEL-01

  • Observed at 16:54:03 Eastern time ET
    Volodymyr Kvashuk v. U.S. Attorney General (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca11-25-11844 / USCOURTS-ca11-25-11844-0

    FAPD-AI: A Ukrainian national entered the United States on a nonimmigrant visa and applied for asylum but was convicted of multiple federal crimes including money laundering, qualifying as an aggravated felony for removal purposes. The Department of Homeland Security issued a final removal order, and the petitioner challenged it pro se. The Eleventh Circuit denied the petition, finding him conclusively removable under immigration law. USCOURTS-SEL-01

  • Observed at 16:54:03 Eastern time ET
    Kashyap Bakhai v. BDO USA, P.C. (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca11-25-12797 / USCOURTS-ca11-25-12797-0

    FAPD-AI: An accounting partner at a professional services firm was terminated and challenged the termination through arbitration, claiming the firm lacked cause and acted in bad faith. The arbitration panel ruled in the partner's favor, finding insufficient evidence for the termination grounds cited. The Eleventh Circuit affirmed the district court's confirmation of the arbitration award, rejecting the firm's arguments that fraud procured the award or that the arbitrators exceeded their authority. USCOURTS-SEL-01

  • Observed at 16:54:02 Eastern time ET
    Darin Whitchurch, et al v. Michael Mulkey, et al (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca11-25-11187 / USCOURTS-ca11-25-11187-0

    FAPD-AI: The appellants sued their house contractor in state court alleging overbilling under a cost-plus contract and lost at trial, then filed a federal RICO claim in a separate lawsuit. The Eleventh Circuit affirmed both orders. USCOURTS-SEL-01

    119 HR 9203 RH: Student Protection and University Accountability Act (opens in a new tab)
    Legislation · govinfo API · BILLS-119hr9203rh

    FAPD-AI: The Student Protection and University Accountability Act requires colleges and universities to establish and publicly disclose processes for investigating complaints alleging discrimination on the basis of race, color, or national origin under Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964. Institutions must provide timely notifications to complainants within specified periods, maintain complaint records, and comply with an annual attestation requirement, with sanctions including ineligibility for federal funding for institutions failing to comply for two consecutive award years. The bill also requires the Office for Civil Rights to provide bimonthly congressional briefings on discrimination complaints received and imposes process reforms on the Office regarding complaint investigations. BILLS-SEL-01

    Federal Register · govinfo API · DEPARTMENT OF DEFENSE · FR-2026-09-09 / 2026-18317

    official summary: The purpose of this supplemental notice of proposed rulemaking is for the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and the Department of the Army (“the agencies”) to supplement and seek additional comment on certain aspects of an earlier proposal, published on November 20, 2025, to revise the regulations defining the scope of waters federally covered under the Clean Water Act in light of the U.S. Supreme Court's 2023 decision in Sackett v. Environmental Protection Agency. As stated in the agencies' November 20, 2025 Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM), the agencies intend for this rulemaking to provide greater regulatory certainty and increase Clean Water Act program predictability and consistency by clarifying the definition of “waters of the United States.” After consideration of the public comments received on the NPRM, the agencies are issuing this notice to supplement the NPRM with additional regulatory options on certain aspects of the proposed rule.     Air Plan Approval; New York; Interstate Transport Requirements for the 2010 SO 2 NAAQS (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AGENCY · FR-2026-09-09 / 2026-18324

    official summary: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA or the Agency) is approving a State Implementation Plan (SIP) submitted by the State of New York for purpose of demonstrating that the State satisfies the interstate transport requirements, also known as the “good neighbor” provision of the Clean Air Act (CAA), for the 2010 1-hour sulfur dioxide (SO 2 ) primary National Ambient Air Quality Standard (NAAQS). Under the good neighbor provision, each State's implementation plan must contain adequate provisions prohibiting the interstate transport of air pollution in amounts that will either contribute significantly to nonattainment, or interfere with maintenance, of the NAAQS in any other State. This action is being taken in accordance with the requirements of the Clean Air Act. FR-SEL-01

    official summary: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is approving a portion of Indiana's State Implementation Plan (SIP) submission regarding the infrastructure requirements in Clean Air Act (CAA) section 110 for the 2015 ozone National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS). The infrastructure requirements are designed to ensure that the structural components of each State's air quality management program are adequate to meet the State's responsibilities under the CAA. The EPA finds that Indiana's infrastructure submission fulfills CAA requirements for a State's SIP to contain adequate provisions prohibiting emissions that will interfere with required visibility protection measures in any other State's SIP.     Improving the Effectiveness of the Robocall Mitigation Database; Call Authentication Trust Anchor; Advanced Methods To… (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · FEDERAL COMMUNICATIONS COMMISSION · FR-2026-09-09 / 2026-18366

    official summary: In this document, the Federal Communications Commission (Commission) proposes steps to strengthen the reliability, integrity, and effectiveness of the Robocall Mitigation Database (RMD or Database) as a core component of its illegal-call prevention framework. The Commission proposed measures aim to ensure that RMD filings are accurate, complete, and current, and to safeguard the Database so that only legitimate, transparent, and accountable providers may enter or remain listed. Specifically, the Commission proposes and seeks comment on measures to clarify which entities are required to file in the RMD, enhance the accuracy and completeness of submitted information, and specify which portions of filings may be publicly disclosed. Additionally, the Commission proposes and seeks comment on new tools to prevent bad actors and noncompliant providers from accessing or remaining in the RMD, including strengthened screening procedures for new filers, improved mechanisms for identifying noncompliant providers, expedited removal processes, and safeguards to prevent unauthorized re-entry into the Database. FR-SEL-02

This proposed AD was prompted by reports of fuel leakage near rib 6 during production pressure testing. An investigation found oversized holes in a certain outboard shear-tie. This proposed AD would require an inspection of the fasteners and fastener holes at rib 6 for discrepancies and applicable on-condition actions. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products. FR-SEL-02

    Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard No. 213a; Child Restraint Systems—Side Impact Protection; Federal Motor Vehicle S… (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION · FR-2026-09-09 / 2026-18380

    official summary: This final rule amends the safety standards for child restraint systems (CRSs). NHTSA is amending Federal motor vehicle safety standard (FMVSS) No. 213a, “Child restraint systems—side impact protection,” to exempt school bus CRSs from the standard's requirements as long as they meet specified labeling requirements; to delay the compliance date from June 30, 2025 to December 5, 2026; to amend the dummy selection requirements so that the Child Restraint Air Bag Interaction twelve-month-old test dummy (CRABI-12MO) will not be used to test forward-facing CRSs; and to amend positioning procedures for that dummy. The first two of these amendments are in response to petitions from CRS manufacturers. NHTSA is also amending FMVSS No. 213, “Child restraint systems” and FMVSS No. 213b, “Child restraint systems; Mandatory applicability beginning December 5, 2026,” to exclude school bus CRSs from the requirements to provide attachments for connection to the vehicle's child restraint anchorage system and to change certain labeling requirements to reflect how school bus child restraints are used. FR-SEL-01

    official summary: NMFS is prohibiting directed fishing for Pacific ocean perch in the Western Aleutian district (WAI) of the Bering Sea and Aleutian Islands management area (BSAI) by vessels participating in the BSAI trawl limited access sector fishery. This action is necessary to prevent exceeding the 2026 total allowable catch (TAC) of Pacific ocean perch in the WAI allocated to vessels participating in the BSAI trawl limited access sector fishery.
